strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) interpret the scriptures on work to foster responsibility, b) discuss virtues related to Christian work ethics, c) choose career paths based on his/her gifts talents and abilities, d) demonstrate a positive attitude towards work in daily activities, e) desire to work hard to achieve
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● in groups discuss why it is important to work hard at home, school and the community ● in pairs share experiences on the chores/roles they perform at home, school, church and the community ● conduct a buzz session on; a lazy person should not eat; 2 Thessalonians 3:10-12 ● in groups, read Proverbs 6:6-11, Proverbs 10:4 Exodus 20:11, Genesis 2:1-3; outline the teachings, and write them on charts or PowerPoint slides for presentation in class ● conduct a library or online research on virtues related to work and share the findings with the class ● compose a poem on,’ God worked, we should also work.’ ● write their career aspirations (what they want to become in the future) on flashcards and share with the class ● in groups brainstorm on requirements for the different careers and how to work towards attaining them
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can you develop a positive attitude towards work?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) elaborate Christian moral values that a young person should uphold in day-to-day life, b) describe forbidden sexual practices outlined in the Bible, c) utilise Christian moral values and life skills that foster sexual purity, d) desire to live a morally upright life as guided by the Bible.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● brainstorm on moral values that youths should uphold to overcome sexual sins ● in groups brainstorm on 1 Corinthians 15:33, 1 Thessalonians 4:3, 1Corinthians 6:13, 1 Corinthians 6:18- 20, Leviticus 11:44, and discuss the moral values outlined ● brainstorm on sexual perversions today and how youths are lured ● in groups read Galatians 5:19 and Leviticus 18:5-18, 20-23, and use PowerPoint slides or charts to list forbidden sexual practices ● in pairs discuss how to avoid getting lured into forbidden sexual practises ● read Romans 1:26-27 and brainstorm on how one can avoid being lured to same- sex relationships ● in groups perform a skit on how to overcome or avoid being lured into sexual perversity
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you live a morally upright life? 2. Why should you maintain sexual purity as a Christian youth?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse qualities portrayed by Deborah as a judge in Israel, b) deduct lessons learnt from the leadership of Judge Deborah, c) appreciate those in leadership by praying for them always.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● in groups, list women leaders (at school, church or in government positions); identify and list good leadership qualities you can emulate from them ● outline leadership qualities portrayed by Deborah as a woman Judge in Israel ● in groups read the story in Judges 4:1-24 and make notes ● watch a movie on, ‘Judge Deborah.’ ● brainstorm on lessons learnt from the leadership of Judge Deborah and make short notes.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How did Deborah portray wisdom as a woman Judge?

strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs to list names of members in their family tree

strands.strand: The Life and Ministry of Jesus Christ
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) elaborate the miracle of raising the Widow’s son at Nain, b) interpret lessons learnt from the miracle for application in day-to-day life, c) model the value of compassion as portrayed by Jesus Christ, d) appreciate God’s power over life and death and the hope of resurrection.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● in pairs share experiences of challenges they have faced as a family (e.g. losing loved ones/close relatives), ● discuss how they coped/cope with grief or loss ● read Luke 7:11-16 and make notes on the raising of the widow’s son ● use a digital device or write on charts how they show compassion to the needy or the suffering ● visit and pray for the sick at home and school ● write John 11:25 on flashcards and meditate on it ● compose a poem on God’s power over sickness and death
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why should you trust in God when faced with challenges? 2. Why is it important to believe in the resurrection as Christians?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe the healing of the ten lepers, b) devise ways of showing gratitude to God in day-to-day life, c) demonstrate faith by praying to God when faced with challenges, d) apply lessons learnt by showing kindness to others.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● in turns read Luke 17:11-19 and make a presentation in class using a chart or a digital device ● in groups role-play the healing of the ten lepers ● in pairs discuss lessons learnt from this miracle and share with the class ● share experiences of how they express gratitude to God and those who show them kindness ● compose a poem to thank God, parents/guardians or a friend and recite it ● in groups compose a song of thanksgiving and sing it in class, the school assembly or during the programme of Pastoral Instruction.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How did the 10 lepers show gratitude to God?

strands.strand: The Life and Ministry of Jesus Christ
strands.subStrand: Parable on prayer A Friend at Midnight
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) elaborate the parable of a friend at midnight, b) interpret lessons learnt from the parable of a friend at midnight for application in day- to-day life, c) Appreciate the parable by praying to God always.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● in pairs brainstorm the meaning of the word parable, write it on flashcards and share with the class ● in pairs share experiences of how they prayed persistently for an issue/challenge ● read Luke 11:5-13 and discuss in groups the parable of a friend at midnight ● role-play the parable of a friend at midnight ● prepare PowerPoint slides or charts on lessons learnt from the parable of a friend at midnight and make a presentation in class ● write a reflection journal on how they pray daily.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why should Christians pray at all times? 2. How do you exercise faith in prayer?

strands.strand: The Life and Ministry of Jesus Christ
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ, b) relate the significance of the bronze serpent to the mission of Jesus Christ, c) deduce lessons learnt from John 3:5-7 and its relevance to the life of a Christian,
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● read John 3:1-16 and make summary notes on Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ ● role-play the story of Nicodemus ● watch a video on Nicodemus’ conversion ● sing a song on Nicodemus’ conversion ● read Numbers 21:4-8 and John 3:14- 15 and brainstorm on how the bronze serpent is related to Jesus Christ and His mission on earth (Luke 4:18-21, Acts 10:38)
strands.inquiryQuestions: How did Nicodemus’ encounter with Christ change his life?

strands.strand: The Life and Ministry of Jesus Christ
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) elaborate Jesus Christ’s triumphant entry into Jerusalem, b) illustrate Jesus Christ’s cleansing of the temple, c) analyse Jesus Christ’s conflict with the Jewish leaders, d) desire to avoid conflicts at home, school and the community.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● share experiences on what happens on Palm Sunday, as practiced by some churches ● watch a video clip on Jesus Christ’s triumphant entry into Jerusalem ● read Luke 19:38, compose and sing a song related to the scripture in class or during the Programme of Pastoral Instruction ● read in turns Luke 19:28-40 and note key points on a chart or use a digital device for presentation in class ● in groups brainstorm on ways the Church premise is misused today ● read Luke 19:45-48 on Jesus Christ’s cleansing of the temple ● discuss lessons learnt from the cleansing of the Temple and make notes ● share experiences on how they resolve conflicts at home, school and the community
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why was Jesus’ triumphant entry into Jerusalem important? 2. Why was Jesus opposed by the Jewish leaders?

strands.strand: The Life and Ministry of Jesus Christ
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the significance of the Lord’s Supper to Christians today, b) describe the events that took place at Mount Olives, c) summarise the events that took place between the arrest and the burial of Jesus Christ, d) discuss the importance of Christ’s resurrection to the Christian faith, e) appreciate Christ’s resurrection as a sign of eternal life.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● in groups conduct a buzz session on the meaning of the Lord's Supper ● share experiences of how they celebrate the Lord's Supper/Lord’s Table/Holy Communion/Eucharist/Sacrament in their churches ● in turns read Luke 22:7-20 and make notes on the Last Supper ● download and watch a video on the events that took place at Mount Olives (Luke 22:39-53) and make notes ● in pairs share experiences on when they were betrayed by close friends or relatives ● discuss lessons they learnt from the betrayal ● take turns to read Luke 22:54-62 on Peter’s betrayal of Jesus Christ ● in groups dramatise Peter’s denial of Jesus Christ
strands.inquiryQuestions: How is the resurrection of Jesus Christ important to Christians today?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) discuss the characteristics of the Early Church, b) describe the miracles performed in the Early Church, c) analyse the story of Paul and Silas and its relevance to Christians today, d) desire to grow spiritually by attending church.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided:  in pairs read and discuss characteristics of the early church, that is, devotion to scriptures, fellowship, prayer, worship, and giving, Acts 2:41-47  in groups visit different churches and interview the priest/pastor/church leaders on how the church today exhibits characteristics of the Early Church, write a report and present it to the class  read Acts 2:43, 5:12, 3:1-16, 5:12-16 on the miracles performed in the Early Church and outline lessons learnt  read Acts 16:16-34, outline lessons learnt and make short notes  choose and sing a worship song familiar to the class  write and keep a journal on church attendance and activities done (a church leader to sign the journal).
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can you apply lessons learnt from the Early Church in your life?

strands.subStrand: The Gifts of the Holy Spirit
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) discuss the teachings of Jesus Christ on the role of the Holy Spirit, b) identify the nine gifts of the Holy Spirit,
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● brainstorm on the role of the Holy Spirit in the life of a Christian ● read John 14:15-26, 16:5-15, Acts 1:7-8 on the role of the Holy Spirit; make notes for presentation in class ● in groups search for the meaning of; Gifts of the Holy Spirit share and findings in class ● Read 1Corithinians 12:8-11 and list the nine gifts of the Holy Spirit
strands.inquiryQuestions: How do you utilize the gifts of the Holy Spirit?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) elaborate the causes and consequences of early marriage today, b) discuss moral values and life skills needed to avoid early marriage, c) analyse Christian approaches to courtship and marriage,
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● conduct a buzz session on the causes of early marriage today ● discuss the consequences of early marriage ● brainstorm on moral values and life skills needed to avoid early marriage ● read, write on flashcards and reflect on 1Timothy 4:12 ● in groups debate the meaning of the word, courtship and share findings with the class ● in pairs discuss qualities to consider when choosing a marriage partner
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is courtship important before marriage?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe biblical teachings on responsible parenthood, b) discuss causes of irresponsible parenting today, c) appraise the role of parents/guardians in shaping the character of their children, d) appreciate good parenting as guided
strands.experiences: The learner is guided: ● use relevant textbooks or internet sources to search for the meaning of responsible parenthood and share findings with the class ● in groups read, Exodus 20:12, Deuteronomy 11:18-21, Psalms 103:13, Proverbs 15:20, Proverbs 22:6, and Colossians 3:21, discuss and write lessons learnt on a chart or use PowerPoint slides for presentation in class ● discuss the causes of irresponsible parenting ● brainstorm on ways of avoiding unplanned families

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify different forms of leisure today, b) analyse how youths misuse leisure today, c) identify Christian moral values needed to avoid alcohol, drug and substance use, d) evaluate the effects of alcohol, drug and substance use on an individual, e) utilise Christian moral
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs brainstorm on the different forms of leisure ● share experiences on how they spend their free time ● in groups discuss why and how youth misuse leisure today ● discuss the effects of alcohol, drug and substance use on an individual and make notes /PowerPoint slides for class presentation ● in pairs write and recite poems on, ‘Alcohol drug, and substance use is detrimental to health’.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why do youths misuse leisure today? 2. How can you avoid idleness?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money and poverty, b) appraise how the love of money can hinder
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● in groups read; Deuteronomy 8:18, Ecclesiastes 5:10-19, Proverbs 15:27, Matthew 6:24-27, discuss and make notes ● in groups read; Proverbs 14:23, 31:8-9, Luke 3:11, Luke 4:18 on Christian views of poverty and make a presentation using charts or digital devices
